content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1 (as on 16.06.2025)
Key Insights

1. Kharif Sowing Status: Kharif sowing data collection has started from 06th June, 2025 and the sowing is in preliminary stage. As on 13th June, 2025, the area sown under Kharif crops is 89.29 lakh ha (including 55.07 lakh ha (105% of normal area) in Sugarcane) as compared to 87.81 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. (The normal area coverage during Kharif is estimated to be more than 1100 lakh ha.) 2. Weather Update: a) Temperature: Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-5°C over Northwest India during next 24 hours and no significant change thereafter. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over Central India during next 24 hours and gradual fall by 2-4°C thereafter during subsequent 5 days. Maximum Temperatures likely to fall by 3-4°C over Northwest India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country. b) Rainfall Distribution: From June 01– 15 June, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 31% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)39%; (ii) Northwest India: (-)38%; (iii) Central India: (-)34%; and South Peninsula: (-) 11%.  Extremely heavy rainfall likely at isolated places over Coastal Karnataka, Konkan & Goa during 16th & 17th June.  Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall activity likely over West, Northwest, East, Northeast India, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Costal Karnataka, North Costal Andhra Pradesh and Lakshadweep; Isolated to scattered rainfall likely over Remaining parts of the country.  Light/moderate rainfall at some/isolated places accompanied with accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds likely over most parts of the country.  Rainfall is likely to be below normal in Northwest India and NE India. Above normal rainfall activity is likely over Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, East M.P., Maharashtra and Odisha.  Monsoon likely to be in active phase with heavy to very heavy rainfall at a few places and extremely heavy falls (>20 cm) at isolated places over south peninsular India and Konkan & Goa till 16th June, 2025. 3. Inputs Situation: a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 12th June 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 55.52 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 30.4% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Kharif 2025, certified seed availability is 178.64 lakh quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 4. content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 3
Details of each Segment
1. RAINFALL  During the week (05th June – 11th June2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long

Period Average (LPA) by 58%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th June to 11th June 2025) is lower than LPA by 34%. Rainfall Forecast:  Overall rainfall activity is likely to be above most parts of the country except south Peninsular India; where below normal rainfall activity is likely during the week. Advance of Southwest Monsoon:  The Northern Limit of Monsoon continues to pass through 17.0°N/55°E, 17.5°N/60°E, 18°N/65°E, 18.5°N/70°E, Mumbai, Ahilyanagar, Adilabad, Bhawanipatna, Puri, Sandhead Island, 23.5°N/89.5°E, Balurghat, 30°N/85°E.  Conditions are favourable for further advancement of Southwest monsoon over some parts of Gujarat, some more parts of Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh & Odisha during next 24 hours; over some parts of West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar and East Uttar Pradesh during subsequent 3 days.

4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

(a) Soil Moisture Observation  Soil moisture during 07 June – 13 June 2025 was better than the average of the past 9 years in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Western M.P, Maharashtra, Karnataka, A.P., Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal.  It was lower than average of past 9 years in Bihar and Eastern UP.
